question: At which replacement does a ship rebuilt part by part stop being the same ship, and which view of identity says so?
finding: On a 46-part galley with the keel counted as 20 planks, half of the original weight has gone after 6 replacements if the frame goes first and after 41 if worn parts go first, while a head count of parts says step 23 either way.
limit: The tool sorts a visitor's mark by the view it agrees with; it cannot say which view of identity is true, and both the part weights and the 50% thresholds are conventions.
